cases.purpose: Prove framed bytes cross a fixture-owned loopback OpenSSH transport, then relay a live remote attach's raw terminal bytes through it.
cases.stdout:
independent-ssh-frame-control=PASS
live-peer-startup-line=PASS
live-peer-receives-raw-input=PASS
live-peer-bytes-delivered-unchanged=PASS
remote-attach-success=PASS
owned-cleanup=PASS
cases.oracle: A fresh unprivileged OpenSSH daemon listens only on loopback with fixture-generated keys and a forced independent BSCR peer. Setup first proves a real OpenSSH client exchanges the exact frames with this peer. The forced peer enters the private case cwd and HOME before its own guard. The positive control queues a complete startup line before a TCSANOW raw transition, proves the peer read the exact line and then exchanges independent exact frames; terminal flags, transition phases, and any exact canonical echo are retained.
cases.comparison: The live candidate must deliver exactly the fixed frontend bytes, write exactly the peer's bytes, and exit successfully: the command its startup line names is an ordinary live attach, which reads and writes raw terminal bytes, so the peer stands in for it on a raw wire. The earlier form expected BSCR frames on this stream, where the serving attach would pass a frame header to the pane as input; frames are checked by the remote-frame cases and by the OpenSSH control here. peer input, output and SSH logs are retained. Candidate streams/status and peer partial input are captured on success and exception paths, with client/server cleanup actions and process outcomes. The candidate must send the exact startup line before the frame branch is exercised. Full candidate output is compared without removing startup echoes or frame bytes.
